standard_prerequisites.name: Effective enumeration and dovetailing
standard_prerequisites.statement: Use disjoint infinite computable vertex/edge sets X,E in HF, a computable order of HF of type omega, an effective list phi_t of partial recursive maps X times E to the finite label set, and a computable stage schedule listing each t infinitely often.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The same-source preceding construction185-193 sets these standard conventions.
standard_prerequisites.use: Enumerate every candidate computable coloring and allocate least unused labels. The nonstandard adversarial forest, reserve invariant and bad local patterns remain solution obligations.

core_obligations: For a greedy label set, enumerate vertices and color all incident half edges while preserving greedy labels on every edge with only one colored endpoint.
For a nongreedy problem, fix a bad finite star pattern for each available subset of labels.
Dovetail all partial computable candidate colorings and maintain separated components carrying sufficiently many reserved half edges of each known label.
At a convergent valid stage, force a previously unseen label and combine reserves using a bad star while retaining a large enough supply in distinct components.

Show at most |Sigma| such active stages are possible for each candidate, while a correct total coloring would force infinitely many; also verify the final forest and incidence relation are computable.

proof_roadmap.step: Effective greedy labeling without computing the actual neighbor-count function.
Initialize candidate-specific forests and the three reserve invariants; detect convergence on finite radius1 neighborhoods.
Use the bad star to force a new label and retain unused components, with a finite reserve budget.
Prove computability/acyclicity and diagonalize by finite versus infinite active-stage counts.

difficulty_reason: The forward implication requires a tailored effective diagonal construction, not merely enumerating vertices. It stores label witnesses in separate components, combines them only through bad star patterns, quantitatively budgets their depletion, and forces a new label at each productive stage. This simultaneously preserves acyclicity and decidable incidence while defeating every total computable coloring, including when the true-edge predicate need not be computable.

compared.difference: The old item is the non-full obstruction on truly regular/highly computable forests, using bad long paths and vertex-multiset exhaustion. The new claim is the complete greedy characterization for all computable forests, using stars and half-edge label exhaustion.

editorial_notes: The counted theorem is the characterization for forests. The author introduces the contrapositive with a stronger tree statement at311-313, but the actual proof explicitly constructs a forest and proves exactly that in Claim356-364. Only the forest conclusion needed by the counted theorem is used; the stronger connectedness assertion is not counted or silently repaired.

The effective-enumeration and least-unused-label conventions referred to as before in315-316 are stated explicitly among the standard prerequisites. The preceding non-full long-path argument is not a premise for this task.

For the finite-reserve choices N0 at322/354 one can make the author free choice of a sufficiently large integer divisible by (2*Delta*|Sigma|)^|Sigma|, when |Sigma|>0, so all divisions in active stages are integral. If Sigma is empty, a valid local coloring never occurs and no active-stage division is executed.
All original mathematical proof lines and the two original diagrams are retained. The continuous-coloring proposition301-307, which is outside this claim, is not used.

review_checkpoints: The global assumption Delta>=2 appears explicitly at62; virtual half edges count toward Delta-regularity, and need not become true edges.
The greedy definition includes k=0, so an empty label alphabet is not vacuously greedy. In the nongreedy construction the active valid-coloring case cannot occur for that alphabet.
Incidence is fixed when a vertex is introduced with Delta incident edges; future joining gives old virtual edges another endpoint but does not change the old vertex incidence list.
Each candidate-specific active stage adds a label to Sigma-prime; if a candidate were total and valid, its finite neighborhood computations would eventually converge after every such stage.

issues_for_independent_review.detail: Check that the full constructed forest suffices for the counted theorem283-285 despite the uncounted stronger tree wording312. No connectedness is required for COMPUTABLE.
Check distinct component reserves, possible repeated bad labels, and the allowed integral N0 choice. These are genuine construction obligations, not provided as assumptions.

editorial_scope: One computable-forest characterization theorem, both directions. The nongreedy forest construction and every reserve/decidability argument form the solution. Standard computability enumeration is allowed. The previously published non-full/higher-computability theorem and the unproved stronger connected-tree wording are not additional claims.
